subject: Planned: regional IO quiesce & fast-path reshuffle (APAC window)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: sarah@cachecorp.com, apioops-support@techpartner.io
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Planned: regional IO quiesce & fast-path reshuffle (APAC window)

Hi Sarah / CacheCorp ops,

Quick heads up: we are scheduling a targeted maintenance window for the APAC region to perform a controlled IO quiesce and a "fast-path" network/driver reshuffle to address an emergent NVMe driver contention pattern we've observed in low-latency workloads. This is a rolling operation designed to avoid broad service downtime, but it will result in brief per-host stalls (30–90s) while we drain and remap IO lanes and atomically swap the optimized driver module.

Planned window (customer-facing):
- Start: 2026-10-09 00:00 UTC
- End: 2026-10-09 06:00 UTC
- Expected per-host impact: single-digit seconds of higher latency then a short stall on drain (target <90s)

What we will do:
- Sequential node quiesce -> flush KV cache to persistent layer -> swap driver module -> rehydrate cache prefix -> functional health check
- Load-aware ordering: hosts serving long-running sessions first, ephemeral hosts last

Customer impact & mitigations:
- API requests routed through multi-path routing; most requests will fall back to warmed replicas with no change. A subset of live sessions may see a brief stall during the host drain.
- We will enable aggressive prefix reuse for sessions flagged as latency-sensitive to reduce rehydration time.

Action items for CacheCorp: please confirm whether you need us to avoid any racks or availability zones in your configuration (we can opt-out specific host sets) and whether you want a pre- or post-window traffic drain on your side.

Runbooks & artifacts attached: 20261007-runbook-fastpath-reshuffle.pdf, kv-cache-preserve-checklist.txt

If you prefer a later date we can reschedule, but the driver fix contains a correctness and performance improvement important for your P95 workloads.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0172

Jonas — thanks for the update.

On Wed, Oct 7, 2026 at 09:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick heads up: we are scheduling a targeted maintenance window for the APAC region...

We appreciate the detail. Two quick Qs from our side:
1) Our model-serving fleet in apac-east has a small set of pinned hosts that handle time-sensitive inference for our payments pipeline. Can you opt those hosts out by host-ID or AZ?
2) How long does the KV cache rehydrate typically take for hot prefixes? Our SLAs are tight for tail latency; even short stalls cascade for us.

If you can opt the pins out, we can run a brief traffic drain ourselves at 23:30 UTC and bring traffic back after you confirm completion. Otherwise we may ask for a one-week delay.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Li
SRE Manager, CacheCorp
sarah@cachecorp.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Sarah Li <sarah@cachecorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned: regional IO quiesce & fast-path reshuffle (APAC window)

Sarah — good questions. Short answers inline.

On Oct 7, 2026, at 13:01, Sarah Li <sarah@cachecorp.com> wrote:
> 1) Can you opt those hosts out by host-ID or AZ?
Yes — we can exclude specific host IDs or entire AZs from the rollout. If you provide host IDs (or confirm the AZs), we'll mark them as opt-out in the orchestration group and they will not be drained.

> 2) How long does KV cache rehydrate typically take for hot prefixes?
Typical warm-prefix rehydrates are on the order of 5–20s for the hottest prefixes. For sessions marked latency-sensitive where we keep aggressive prefix reuse, we expect rehydrates closer to 3–8s. The longest tail we measured in the most-misaligned scenario was ~65s, but with the new driver path and our pre-warm heuristics the tail is expected <30s for 99.9% of prefixes.

Planned safeguards we will apply for CacheCorp:
- Exclude pinned host IDs you list (no quiesce on those hosts)
- Pre-window pre-warm: we will pin the top-50 prefixes for your account across nearby replicas 30 minutes before the window
- If you opt in, we will coordinate a CacheCorp-initiated traffic drain at 23:30 UTC before our start time (we'll confirm when the drain is complete)

Marcus will take lead on orchestration and logging; Hannah will run the post-change regressions and smoke tests. Attaching the lightweight checklist for your ops team to review.

Regards,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Production Reliability, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick plan update and confirmation:

1) CacheCorp opt-out: Sarah, we will exclude the host IDs you sent (cc'd Marcus to confirm group assignment). Those hosts will not be drained.
2) Pre-warm: we will pin your top-50 prefixes 30 minutes prior as requested and enable the aggressive prefix-reuse policy.
3) Traffic drain: we confirm you can run a drain at 23:30 UTC on 2026-10-09; please signal completion to ops@redwood.ai and we'll start the first shard at 00:00 UTC.
4) Post-window: Hannah will run the regression suite and send a postmortem within 48 hours if anything anomalous appears.

We will also publish a short incident log to your shared drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/cachecorp/fastpath-reshuffle-20261009 (will be created prior to the window).

If anything changes we'll escalate; otherwise we will proceed with the above schedule.

Jonas
